chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Dawud ibn Sulayman al-Kufi, from Abi Bakr al-Hadrami, who said:

A man from my household became ill, so I came to visit him, and I said to him: O son of my brother, I have some advice for you; will you accept it? He said: Yes. So I said: Say, “I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, having no partner.” So he testified to that. Then I said: And say, “And that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.” So he testified to that. Then I said: This will not benefit you unless it is from you with certainty. So he stated that he held it with certainty.

Then I said to him: Say, “I bear witness that Ali is his legatee, and he is the successor after him, and the Imam whose obedience is divinely obligated after him.” So he testified to that. Then I said to him: You will not benefit from that until it is from you with certainty. So he stated that he held it with certainty. Then I named for him the Imams عليهم السلام one after another, and he affirmed that and stated that he was upon certainty. Not long after that, the man passed away, and his family grieved for him with intense grief.

He said: So I stayed away from them, then I came to them after that and saw a fine state of consolation. I said: How are you finding yourselves? How is your consolation, O woman? She said: By Allah, we were indeed struck by a tremendous calamity in the death of so-and-so, may Allah have mercy on him. But among the things that made me feel at ease regarding him was a dream that I saw last night. I said: And what was that dream? She said: I saw so-and-so — meaning the deceased — alive and unharmed. So I said: So-and-so? She said: Yes. Then I said to him: Had you been dead? He said: Yes, but I was saved by words that Abu Bakr prompted me with, and were it not for that, I would nearly have perished.

key_terms.أَشْهَدُ: I bear witness; the formula of testimony recited to affirm belief.
key_terms.الْأَئِمَّةَ عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ: the Imams عليهم السلام, named one after another.
key_terms.الْإِمَامُ الْمُفْتَرَضُ الطَّاعَةِ: the Imam whose obedience is divinely obligatory.
key_terms.نَجَوْتُ: I was saved; deliverance attributed to the prompted words.
key_terms.وَصِيُّهُ: his legatee; the designated successor of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم.
key_terms.يَقِينٍ: certainty; firm conviction without doubt, required for true benefit.

ai.seo_question: What should be recited to a dying person in Shia hadith, and why is certainty in it important?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates the تلقين of a dying man with testimony to tawhid, the رسالَة of Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and the wilayah and Imamate of Amir al-Mu'minin عليٌّ عليه السلام and the Imams عليهم السلام, with emphasis that these declarations benefit only when held with certainty. After his death, a dream is reported in which the deceased says he was saved by these prompted words.
